text:
Priya: Heads up — AcmeHealth's security team asked for a completed CAIQ (CCM) + an explicit shared-responsibility mapping for Dedicated and Private deployments. They specifically want clear answers for: BYOK/HSM support, encryption at rest, network isolation (VPC), logging/retention, incident response, and any contract hooks. Need a draft to send back by EOD tomorrow (POC will include PHI).

Jordan: I can draft. Quick clarifying Qs: for Dedicated we support customer-managed KMS (BYOK) and HSM-backed keys if they provision hardware or we enable HSM-backed KMS in their VPC — correct? Hosted uses Redwood-managed KMS by default. Do they require HSM attestation/PKCS11 specifics?

Marta: They asked for a one-page shared-responsibility table too. Column layout: Control | Redwood responsibility | Customer responsibility. I'll make that after Jordan's CAIQ snippets.

Alex: Ping legal about DPA + BAA (HIPAA). Also need to confirm whether the POC will use synthetic PHI or redacted real PHI. That affects the responses we give for backups and retention.

Jordan: Answering Qs: yes, Dedicated and Private support BYOK. For Private (on-prem/VPC) customers can bring their own HSM or KMS; we integrate with customer KMS via standard APIs. Hosted = Redwood-managed KMS (multi-tenant) by default, but we offer Dedicated-reserved clusters where BYOK is possible. HSM-backed keys require contract amendment and operational review.

sec-bot: Draft CAIQ guidance (internal): https://internal.redwood/security/caiq-answers v1.2 :lock:

Marta: Putting a first-pass CAIQ/Shared-resp draft below, please review and flag contract items. I'll convert to CAIQ matrix after approvals.

```
CCM-EN-01 (Encryption - data at rest):
- Redwood: Encrypts all customer data at rest using AES-256. For Hosted, keys are managed by Redwood KMS (multi-tenant).
- Customer: For Hosted, customers may request Dedicated or Private deployment to use customer-managed keys (BYOK). For Dedicated/Private, customers may provide KMS or HSM; Redwood integrates via standard KMS APIs. HSM-backed keys (FIPS 140-2/3 modules) require a contractual amendment and ops review.

CCM-EN-02 (Encryption - data in transit):
- Redwood: All in-transit communications TLS 1.2+ (recommend 1.3). Mutual-TLS or customer TLS termination available for Private deployments.

CCM-PR-01 (Identity & Access):
- Redwood: Service side RBAC, least privilege, service-to-service auth. We store access logs and rotate service credentials periodically.
- Customer: Responsible for user identity provider (IdP), SSO, MFA. Customers must manage end-user accounts and their IdP policies.

CCM-LO-01 (Logging & Monitoring):
- Redwood: Application and infrastructure logs captured, retention defaults: 90 days in hosted. Extended retention available as paid add-on. Audit logs can be exported to customer S3/Event Hubs in Dedicated/Private.

CCM-IR-01 (Incident Response):
- Redwood: We maintain an incident response program, SOC2-aligned processes, notify customers per SLA. For Hosted, Redwood leads containment for service-side incidents; for Private/on-prem, customer leads local containment and notifies Redwood where relevant.

Notes on shared responsibility (example rows):
- Network isolation: Redwood configures service networking; customer configures VPC peering, security groups and their firewall.
- Backups: Redwood maintains encrypted backups for service metadata; customers are responsible for their exported data copies and retention if required by policy.

Contract flags: BYOK/HSM = contract amendment; data residency guarantees = SOW; PHI handling in POC = BAA required.
```

Priya: This is great. Two small edits: (1) For logs retention, call out that audit exports are available for Dedicated within 24h. (2) For incident response wording, be explicit: "Redwood notifies customers within 2 hours of a confirmed breach impacting customer data."

Jordan: Updated per Priya: added audit export timing and the 2-hour notification SLA for confirmed breaches. Marked BYOK/HSM and BAA as contract items.

Marta: I'll turn this into the CAIQ CSV + the one-page shared-resp table and attach SOC2/ISO certs. Draft email for AcmeHealth: short cover + attached CAIQ, shared table, certs, and note about contract items (BYOK/HSM, BAA). Want me to send or should Alex/Legal?

Alex: Legal to send the BAA/contract bits. If you can send the technical package (CAIQ + table + certs) to their security contact that'd speed things up — copy me and legal.

Jordan: I'll sign off the technical package now and upload to the secure share. Sending to AcmeHealth security contact in ~20m, CC legal + Priya. :thumbsup:
